doc.title: Data Types
doc.para: Data Types In TJS2, variables do not have "types", but they do have types internally. Rather than saying they do not have types, it is more accurate to say that types are handled automatically/dynamically. Internal types include void, integer type, real number type, string type, object type, and octet sequence type.

void void represents representing nothing (its meaning is different from JavaScript). Newly declared variables are void. To compare void values with each other, use the === (identity) operator. The typeof operator returns "void" for this.

Integer Type TJS2 can handle 64-bit precision integers as the integer type. Integers are usually treated as signed integers, but as the sole exception, the >>> operator treats the left operand as an unsigned integer. The typeof operator returns "Integer" for this.
Real Number Type TJS2 can handle 64-bit precision real numbers ( double-precision real numbers ) as the real number type. The typeof operator returns "Real" for this.

String Type TJS2 can handle null-terminated strings with no length limit. A null-terminated string means that the string is handled under the assumption that it ends with \0. Character encoding uses wide characters (usually UNICODE), but whether it uses 16-bit wide characters or 32-bit wide characters depends on the environment where TJS2 was compiled. For example, it is 16-bit on Windows, but 32-bit on Solaris or Linux. The typeof operator returns "String" for this.

Object Type The object type is a type that holds an object. In addition to objects allocated with the new operator, functions, classes, property objects, etc. are all of the object type. The typeof operator returns "Object" for this.
Unlike TJS or JavaScript, TJS2's object type internally holds two pointers: a pointer to the object itself, and a pointer to the context object in which it should be used, enabling so-called closures. The operator that modifies this context part is the incontextof operator.

Octet Sequence Type The octet sequence type is a type for handling 8-bit wide data sequences (octet sequences). It is primarily a type for handling binary data. The typeof operator returns "Octet" for this.
